response.answer: Nonstationary breakpoints in multi-agent systems can be local for individual agents, and this affects the regret decomposition by introducing additional terms for each agent's specific change counts. The global change assumption simplifies regret analysis but local changes complicate it.

results.title: How we can all be Agents of Change
results.content: Thought Leadership in Project Management and Professional Development # How we can all be Agents of Change **By Lucy Grimwade**January 22, 2025 Let’s face it—change is hard. Whether it’s a new system at work, a company restructure, or even moving house, change disrupts our sense of comfort and control. In fact, change often feels like climbing a steep hill while carrying the weight of uncertainty. But the truth is, change is inevitable. Change Curve (Kubler-Ross, 1966) Originally developed by Elisabeth Kübler-Ross to describe stages of grief, it’s now widely used in change management to illustrate the emotional journey we go through when faced with change. ## So, what does it mean to be a change agent? Simply put, a change agent is someone who **champions and drives change**. Change agents inspire others, challenge the status quo, and bring people together to make things happen. The good news is*, **we can all be agents of change.*** Advocacy doesn’t require a job title or a formal mandate; it starts with mindset. Change isn’t about tearing things down; it’s about building something better. People are more likely to support change when they feel involved in shaping it. Sometimes, resistance isn’t about the change itself but the fear of what it means. Actions speak louder than words, and people are more likely to embrace change when they see its benefits in action. Ultimately, we’re all capable of driving positive change, no matter our role or level of influence. The secret lies in recognising that change isn’t something that happens to us; it’s something we can actively shape. By embracing the inevitability of change and stepping into the role of change agent, we can transform not only our workplaces but also ourselves. ## **Lucy Grimwade** Lucy Grimwade leans into the future of work, positioning herself with a diverse portfolio career across the theme of Change and Transformation. She is a consultant, qualified coach, mentor, author as well as an experienced trainer and public speaker — providing guidance and skills for groups and individuals on subjects that include (but not limited to) change management, career development and personal &/ business transformation.

results.title: Choosing Change Agents: It’s Not All About Position - AlignOrg
results.content: # Choosing Change Agents: It’s Not All About Position. A common assumption in organizations when choosing change agents is that because a person holds a position of authority or influence in the organization, they will automatically be the right person to take on a change leadership or change agent role. This is a natural thing to believe, because being in a position of leadership does give a person a certain amount of leverage or influence that can be advantageous in leading change transformations. And sometimes, it does indeed make sense for these people to take on the change agent role. ### What to look for when choosing change agents. Part of being a change agent is having influence with people and across different parts of an organization. But change agents can come from many different positions within the organization, or even outside of it. More important than position when choosing change agents is to choose people who have the innate ability to understand change and to act in ways that facilitate it. So, how do you choose a good change agent when working on an organization transformation? What characteristics should you look for in potential agents of change? Regardless, good change agents are typically people who have earned the respect of others in the organization. * **Good teachers and communicators.** A great change agent is also somebody who is able to connect the change with how work needs to be done. Whether it’s through positional power or just through their connections, the change agent should be able to point people in the transformation to others in the organization who can assist in influencing and implementing change. A change leader’s influence entails more than just positional power. Those who are leading organization transformations do need to take into account the importance of positional power when choosing change agents to assist with an organization transformation. However, it’s just as important to consider the intangible things people in any position can bring to the table during times of change. Sometimes, it’s these intangible characteristics more so than hierarchical positioning that makes for an effective change agent.

results.title: 5 Qualities All Effective Change Agents Have | MSU Online
results.content: Home » Resources » Strategic Leadership and Management » Qualities of Effective Change Agents. # Qualities of Effective Change Agents. Change management has in recent years shifted from a specialty to be more of a leadership quality that affects how companies and teams adapt to shifting marketplaces and continue daily operations. Whereas change management used to primarily focus on operational and/or process improvements and cost-effectiveness, it is now something that managers are using to think about how things get done regardless of institutional hierarchy. Organizations are looking to change agents to execute new processes and help employees adjust to new ways of doing things. ## What is a Change Agent? Change agents can be managers or employees, or external consultants hired to facilitate initiatives. Internal change agents have the advantage of being familiar with an organization’s history, operations, and people, while external change agents can provide a fresh perspective without the influence of a firm’s traditions and culture, according to Fred C. Whether an organization appoints internal change agents, hires outside consultants or does a combination of both scenarios, “the success of any change effort depends heavily on the quality and workability of the relationship between the change agent and the key decision makers within the organization,” states Lunenburg. ## 5 Qualities All Effective Change Agents Have. Today, playing the role of a change agent has never been more important. If changes are not conducted smoothly and regularly, what would be milestones in a company’s growth could become morale disasters full of missed objectives and a lack of commitment from the people necessary to make change happen. In order to become a truly effective change agent, look to develop these five qualities:. Besides staying abreast of what is happening both inside and outside of the industry, gaining new knowledge through online master and professional certificate programs can help support change agent development. In creating change, it’s often helpful to tie specific priorities to the overall business goals. Effective change agents are able to explore perspectives and take them into account when looking for solutions. ***Develop yourself as the change agent your organization needs with MSU’s online Strategic Leadership & Management Certificates.***.

results.title: How can you get change agents and stakeholders to work together?
results.content: How can you get change agents and stakeholders to work together? But how can you get change agents and stakeholders to work together effectively? Do this, and your change agents and stakeholders will work better together. A third essential strategy to get change agents and stakeholders to work together is to build trust and rapport among them. Change agents can build trust and rapport with stakeholders by being honest, transparent, and respectful, by listening actively and empathetically, by acknowledging and addressing their concerns and emotions, and by recognizing and appreciating their efforts and achievements. Similarly, stakeholders can build trust and rapport with change agents by being open, cooperative, and constructive, by expressing their needs and expectations clearly, and by showing commitment and flexibility. Open and transparent, frequent communication will build trust and rapport between the change agents and stakeholders. 🔹Strategic Finance and Transformation Leader🔹Expert in Regulatory Reporting, Change Management and Operational Excellence🔹Global Stakeholders 🔹Li Top Leadership/Change Management Voice 2024 Building Trust and Rapport is the essence of being able to do all other steps, To do that: Understand the wider and common goal of the organisation Understand how this change is helping achieving that Goal How it's going to help key stakeholders How all the parties are aligned towards common goals How much time or effort you need from stakeholders How it's going to change people's daily work or processes How to help them understand the impact of change in simplest terms What benefits they are going to get once change is implemented Appreciate their concerns and address them effectively How to hand hold or train them to adopt that change Take their feedback in a positive way to improve the solution A fourth vital strategy to get change agents and stakeholders to work together is to communicate effectively and frequently. A fifth crucial strategy to get change agents and stakeholders to work together is to manage conflicts and issues that may arise during the change process. Change agents and stakeholders need to manage conflicts and issues by identifying and addressing them early, by using constructive and respectful language, by focusing on the facts and the common goals, and by seeking win-win solutions that balance the needs and interests of all parties.
